name: Padon
overview: Padon was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant indicates his participation in the religious duties associated with the Levitical priesthood during the post-exilic period. Scripture mentions him specifically in the context of the return from exile.
namesAndTitles: The name Padon is a proper name meaning 'ransom.' This meaning reflects a theological concept of redemption, though the name itself was not given by God according to the record in Ezra 2:44.
familyAndRelationships: Padon is identified as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe entrusted with temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not provide further details about his family or personal relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Padon's significance lies in his role as a temple servant within the Levitical community during the restoration of worship after the Babylonian exile. His mention in Ezra 2:44 highlights the continuity of Levitical service and the reestablishment of the temple ministry under God's providence. As a Levite involved in temple duties, Padon represents the faithful remnant committed to God's covenant and worship.
